subject: Setting the priors for the SPDE

messages.author: 21e2646f0cc9f243
messages.subject: Setting the priors for the SPDE
parts:
Hello,

I wanted to enquire which rule should one use when setting the priors for the range and sigma in the SPDE. I have noted changing these values (the priors) affects the results one obtains after fitting the model. I have made sure that my units are in km.
```
nu <- 1 # Matern smoothness parameter
alpha <- 2
r0 <- 0.5
#Matern SPDE model object using inla.pcmatern
spde <- inla.spde2.pcmatern(mesh = mesh,
                            alpha = alpha,
                            constr = TRUE,
                            prior.range = c(1, 0.01), # P(range < 1) = .01
                            prior.sigma = c(5, 0.01) # P(sigma > 5) = .01
                            )
```
Also, I would like to know if there's any rule of thumb when setting the priors for the precision of the random noise term

```
hyper.prec = list(theta = list(prior = "pc.prec", param = c(5, 0.01)))
```

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Setting the priors for the SPDE
parts:
Dear Brian, 

We certainly can help you on how to set a specific prior. However, please consider that prior distributions on a model are to formally add the personal (or expert) prior knowledge on that. Therefore I cannot set a prior distribution for your problem because I do not have a prior knowledge about it.

On how to set a prior. For example, if you want to use the PC-priors (in the inla.spde2.pcmater() model builder function) you can play with the two probability statements. The paper for this is in this link https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/01621459.2017.1415907

For the (practical) range parameter, you use P(range < reference) = a. Some use it to set a low probability (small a) for a small range (small reference). Some use median.

For the marginal standard deviation (sigma) the probability statement is P(sigma > reference) = a. Some use median and some use a (relatively) big reference along with a small probability.

In summary, if we both were to solve the same problem, we may use different prior and therefore the posterior will differ. When the information from the data dominates, the difference from the prior is negligible on the posterior.

I hope this helps,
Elias

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Setting the priors for the SPDE
parts:
There is no unique way to account for this kind of prior knowledge. I would use that as a prior median.
                            prior.range = c(50, 0.5), # P(range < 50) = .5
                            prior.sigma = c(sqrt(0.2), 0.5) # P(sigma > sqrt(0.2)) = .5
however, you can use it in another way. The best would be to consider the full marginal posterior.

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Setting the priors for the SPDE
parts:
From the methodological aspect, I recommend starting with
https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2211675322000057
and then to consider the references therein.

For applications, there is a tutorial-book. From the (https://www.r-inla.org/) you click in LearnMore, then in Books and you will see the book link along with links for the gitbook version and the code to reproduce the examples. However, please remember that it used an old (around 6 years old now) inla version. The recent ones improved a lot. All the examples there can be updated with modern inla however mostly all of them still work. Several examples were along the line of using the SPDE models as a model component in more complex models and still serve as inspiration. 

The main recent developments in terms of applications of SPDE models are with the inlabru package (https://github.com/inlabru-org/inlabru) and you can find practical tutorials within the "Articles" section. Also, consider the rSPDE (https://github.com/davidbolin/rSPDE/) which deals with the estimation of the smoothness parameter as well.

best regards,
Elias

Thanks a lot. Is there any book/paper you would recommend that elaborates more about the SPDE approach?
